papers.title: MCFST: Spatial domain identification method based on multi-view graph convolutional network and graph fusion network
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The emergence of spatial transcriptomics, which integrates spatial and gene expression information, has greatly advanced research in disease mechanisms and developmental biology. A core task in this field is spatial domain identification, which reveals regions with shared molecular signatures and histological features, thereby facilitating the study of tissue function and pathology. Although existing methods have achieved promising performance, many of them still face limitations in effectively integrating heterogeneous information from multiple views, such as gene expression, spatial coordinates, and spatially informed expression profiles. In particular, discrepancies across views may lead to inconsistent representations and distorted similarity relationships, which can reduce the accuracy and robustness of spatial domain recognition. Results To address these limitations, we propose MCFST, a graph neural network framework that integrates multi-view graph convolution with a fusion module guided by mutual information maximization. By incorporating diverse views of spatial data and aligning their representations, MCFST effectively captures latent patterns and achieves robust domain recognition. We evaluated MCFST against state-of-the-art methods on two simulated datasets with varying sparsity and noise levels, as well as three real spatial transcriptomics datasets. Results show that MCFST consistently outperforms baselines in spatial domain identification, highlighting its robustness and efficiency. Moreover, spatially variable genes detected from MCFST-derived domains exhibited clear spatial expression patterns, further confirming the accuracy and utility of MCFST. Availability The code implementation of the MCFST algorithm is publicly available at https://github.com/dw666666/MCFST
papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: The emergence of spatial transcriptomics, which integrates spatial and gene expression information, has greatly advanced research in disease mechanisms and developmental biology. A core task in this field is spatial domain identification, which reveals regions with shared molecular signatures and histological features, thereby facilitating the study of tissue function and pathology. Although existing methods have achieved promising performance, many of them still face limitations in effectively integrating heterogeneous information from multiple views, such as gene expression, spatial coordinates, and spatially informed expression profiles. In particular, discrepancies across views may lead to inconsistent representations and distorted similarity relationships, which can reduce the accuracy and robustness of spatial domain recognition.

RESULTS: To address these limitations, we propose MCFST, a graph neural network framework that integrates multi-view graph convolution with a fusion module guided by mutual information maximization. By incorporating diverse views of spatial data and aligning their representations, MCFST effectively captures latent patterns and achieves robust domain recognition. We evaluated MCFST against state-of-the-art methods on two simulated datasets with varying sparsity and noise levels, as well as three real spatial transcriptomics datasets. Results show that MCFST consistently outperforms baselines in spatial domain identification, highlighting its robustness and efficiency. Moreover, spatially variable genes detected from MCFST-derived domains exhibited clear spatial expression patterns, further confirming the accuracy and utility of MCFST.

AVAILABILITY: The code implementation of the MCFST algorithm is publicly available at https://github.com/dw666666/MCFST.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：空间转录组学的出现整合了空间信息与基因表达数据，这一技术显著推动了疾病机制研究及发育生物学的发展。
llm_highlights_zh: 该领域的核心任务是空间域识别，这一技术能够揭示那些具有相同分子特征与组织学特性的区域，从而有助于深入研究组织的功能与病理机制。
尽管现有方法已经取得了令人满意的效果，但它们在有效整合来自不同来源的异构信息方面仍存在诸多局限性——这些信息包括基因表达数据、空间坐标信息以及基于空间信息的表达谱分析结果等。
特别是，不同视角之间的差异可能会导致表示结果不一致，进而使相似性关系出现扭曲，这些因素都会降低空间域识别的准确性与可靠性。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
空间转录组学技术的出现，通过整合空间信息与基因表达数据，极大地推动了疾病机制研究与发育生物学的发展。该领域的核心任务之一是识别具有共同分子特征及组织结构的区域，从而有助于深入探讨组织功能与病理变化。尽管现有方法已取得了显著进展，但它们在有效整合来自基因表达、空间坐标等多维数据的异构信息方面仍存在局限——尤其是不同数据源之间的差异可能导致表征结果不一致，进而影响空间域识别的准确性与可靠性。  

为解决这些问题，我们提出了MCFST这一基于图神经网络的框架。该模型结合了多视图图卷积技术，并通过互信息最大化机制对各种空间数据的表示进行协同优化，从而有效捕捉潜在的模式并实现稳健的领域识别。我们在两个具有不同稀疏度与噪声水平的模拟数据集，以及三个真实的空间转录组学数据集上对MCFST进行了测试。结果表明，MCFST在空间域识别方面始终优于现有方法，其鲁棒性与高效性得到了充分验证；此外，通过MCFST识别的空间变异基因也展现了清晰的空间表达规律，进一步证明了该方法的准确性与实用性。  

**代码获取**  
MCFST算法的源代码已公开发布，可访问以下链接获取：  
https://github.com/dw666666/MCFST

all_papers.title: MCFST: Spatial domain identification method based on multi-view graph convolutional network and graph fusion network
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The emergence of spatial transcriptomics, which integrates spatial and gene expression information, has greatly advanced research in disease mechanisms and developmental biology. A core task in this field is spatial domain identification, which reveals regions with shared molecular signatures and histological features, thereby facilitating the study of tissue function and pathology. Although existing methods have achieved promising performance, many of them still face limitations in effectively integrating heterogeneous information from multiple views, such as gene expression, spatial coordinates, and spatially informed expression profiles. In particular, discrepancies across views may lead to inconsistent representations and distorted similarity relationships, which can reduce the accuracy and robustness of spatial domain recognition. Results To address these limitations, we propose MCFST, a graph neural network framework that integrates multi-view graph convolution with a fusion module guided by mutual information maximization. By incorporating diverse views of spatial data and aligning their representations, MCFST effectively captures latent patterns and achieves robust domain recognition. We evaluated MCFST against state-of-the-art methods on two simulated datasets with varying sparsity and noise levels, as well as three real spatial transcriptomics datasets. Results show that MCFST consistently outperforms baselines in spatial domain identification, highlighting its robustness and efficiency. Moreover, spatially variable genes detected from MCFST-derived domains exhibited clear spatial expression patterns, further confirming the accuracy and utility of MCFST. Availability The code implementation of the MCFST algorithm is publicly available at https://github.com/dw666666/MCFST
all_papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: The emergence of spatial transcriptomics, which integrates spatial and gene expression information, has greatly advanced research in disease mechanisms and developmental biology. A core task in this field is spatial domain identification, which reveals regions with shared molecular signatures and histological features, thereby facilitating the study of tissue function and pathology. Although existing methods have achieved promising performance, many of them still face limitations in effectively integrating heterogeneous information from multiple views, such as gene expression, spatial coordinates, and spatially informed expression profiles. In particular, discrepancies across views may lead to inconsistent representations and distorted similarity relationships, which can reduce the accuracy and robustness of spatial domain recognition.

RESULTS: To address these limitations, we propose MCFST, a graph neural network framework that integrates multi-view graph convolution with a fusion module guided by mutual information maximization. By incorporating diverse views of spatial data and aligning their representations, MCFST effectively captures latent patterns and achieves robust domain recognition. We evaluated MCFST against state-of-the-art methods on two simulated datasets with varying sparsity and noise levels, as well as three real spatial transcriptomics datasets. Results show that MCFST consistently outperforms baselines in spatial domain identification, highlighting its robustness and efficiency. Moreover, spatially variable genes detected from MCFST-derived domains exhibited clear spatial expression patterns, further confirming the accuracy and utility of MCFST.

AVAILABILITY: The code implementation of the MCFST algorithm is publicly available at https://github.com/dw666666/MCFST.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：空间转录组学的出现整合了空间信息与基因表达数据，这一技术显著推动了疾病机制研究及发育生物学的发展。
llm_highlights_zh: 该领域的核心任务是空间域识别，这一技术能够揭示那些具有相同分子特征与组织学特性的区域，从而有助于深入研究组织的功能与病理机制。
尽管现有方法已经取得了令人满意的效果，但它们在有效整合来自不同来源的异构信息方面仍存在诸多局限性——这些信息包括基因表达数据、空间坐标信息以及基于空间信息的表达谱分析结果等。
特别是，不同视角之间的差异可能会导致表示结果不一致，进而使相似性关系出现扭曲，这些因素都会降低空间域识别的准确性与可靠性。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
空间转录组学技术的出现，通过整合空间信息与基因表达数据，极大地推动了疾病机制研究与发育生物学的发展。该领域的核心任务之一是识别具有共同分子特征及组织结构的区域，从而有助于深入探讨组织功能与病理变化。尽管现有方法已取得了显著进展，但它们在有效整合来自基因表达、空间坐标等多维数据的异构信息方面仍存在局限——尤其是不同数据源之间的差异可能导致表征结果不一致，进而影响空间域识别的准确性与可靠性。  

为解决这些问题，我们提出了MCFST这一基于图神经网络的框架。该模型结合了多视图图卷积技术，并通过互信息最大化机制对各种空间数据的表示进行协同优化，从而有效捕捉潜在的模式并实现稳健的领域识别。我们在两个具有不同稀疏度与噪声水平的模拟数据集，以及三个真实的空间转录组学数据集上对MCFST进行了测试。结果表明，MCFST在空间域识别方面始终优于现有方法，其鲁棒性与高效性得到了充分验证；此外，通过MCFST识别的空间变异基因也展现了清晰的空间表达规律，进一步证明了该方法的准确性与实用性。  

**代码获取**  
MCFST算法的源代码已公开发布，可访问以下链接获取：  
https://github.com/dw666666/MCFST

**结果**：为克服这些局限，我们提出了MCFST这一图神经网络框架。该框架结合了多视图图卷积技术，并通过互信息最大化机制设计了融合模块，从而有效整合了多种空间数据的表征信息并实现了对目标区域的精准识别。我们在两个具有不同稀疏度与噪声水平的模拟数据集，以及三个真实的空间转录组学数据集上对MCFST进行了性能评估。结果表明，MCFST在空间区域识别方面的表现始终优于现有方法，其鲁棒性与效率得到了充分验证。此外，通过MCFST识别的空间变异基因也展现了明确的表达模式，进一步证明了该方法的准确性与实用性。

all_papers.primary_summary:
空间转录组学的出现整合了空间信息与基因表达数据，极大地推动了疾病机制及发育生物学的研究进展。该领域的核心任务之一是识别具有共同分子特征与组织学特性的区域，从而有助于深入研究组织的功能与病理变化。尽管现有方法已取得了显著成效，但它们在有效整合来自基因表达、空间坐标以及基于空间信息的表达谱等多源异构数据方面仍存在局限性。尤其是不同数据源之间的差异可能导致表征结果不一致，进而扭曲相似性分析的结果，从而降低空间区域识别的准确性与可靠性。
为克服这些局限，我们提出了MCFST这一图神经网络框架。该框架结合了多视图图卷积技术，并通过互信息最大化机制设计了融合模块，从而有效整合了多种空间数据的表征信息并实现了对目标区域的精准识别。我们在两个具有不同稀疏度与噪声水平的模拟数据集，以及三个真实的空间转录组学数据集上对MCFST进行了性能评估。结果表明，MCFST在空间区域识别方面的表现始终优于现有方法，其鲁棒性与效率得到了充分验证。此外，通过MCFST识别的空间变异基因也展现了明确的表达模式，进一步证明了该方法的准确性与实用性。

代码获取：MCFST算法的源代码已公开发布在https://github.com/dw666666/MCFST地址上。

补充信息：相关补充数据可在线查阅Bioinformatics数据库。
all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: The emergence of spatial transcriptomics, which integrates spatial and gene expression information, has greatly advanced research in disease mechanisms and developmental biology. A core task in this field is spatial domain identification, which reveals regions with shared molecular signatures and histological features, thereby facilitating the study of tissue function and pathology. Although existing methods have achieved promising performance, many of them still face limitations in effectively integrating heterogeneous information from multiple views, such as gene expression, spatial coordinates, and spatially informed expression profiles. In particular, discrepancies across views may lead to inconsistent representations and distorted similarity relationships, which can reduce the accuracy and robustness of spatial domain recognition.

RESULTS: To address these limitations, we propose MCFST, a graph neural network framework that integrates multi-view graph convolution with a fusion module guided by mutual information maximization. By incorporating diverse views of spatial data and aligning their representations, MCFST effectively captures latent patterns and achieves robust domain recognition. We evaluated MCFST against state-of-the-art methods on two simulated datasets with varying sparsity and noise levels, as well as three real spatial transcriptomics datasets. Results show that MCFST consistently outperforms baselines in spatial domain identification, highlighting its robustness and efficiency. Moreover, spatially variable genes detected from MCFST-derived domains exhibited clear spatial expression patterns, further confirming the accuracy and utility of MCFST.

AVAILABILITY: The code implementation of the MCFST algorithm is publicly available at https://github.com/dw666666/MCFST.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
